negative_reviews.author: Luca Cabrini
negative_reviews.text:
I ordered the "spicy seafood ramen." I knew it would be spicy, but I certainly did not expect the noodles to taste like supermarket instant noodles rather than fresh ones. The salmon was dry, and the other piece of fish was chewy and rubbery and dish itself smell like old food.

Even though I left my dish almost untouched, no one from the staff checked on us or asked if everything was okay. On top of that, the staff were extremely loud. While we were still eating, they started emptying bins and left bags of rubbish behind our table because they were getting ready to close. It was very noisy and showed little consideration for customers who were still dining.

This was my fourth visit. The first two times were shortly after they opened, and I have to say the quality has dropped significantly since then.

When it was time to pay, the manager asked if I wanted to take the food home. After I explained that I hadn't enjoyed the meal, her only response was, "Oh, okay, sorry," before walking away. Honestly, I wasn't expecting a discount or for the dish to be removed from the bill. I simply expected a bit more care and attention towards the customer.

I truly believe this will be my last visit here (even though you'll probably think, "Okay, no problem"). It's disappointing to see how much things have changed.

negative_reviews.author: Levi Litman
negative_reviews.text:
Went in last week with a group of 5. Food was actually pretty nice. However the service was horrific. When ordering we asked the waitress if the food could all come out together as we had a mix of smaller sharing plates and larger dishes. The waitress assured us this would be fine.

This was in fact not the case and there was a 30 minute wait before our Sushi came in comparison to the rest of the dishes. The other dishes were a slightly staggered delay which was fine. But this service, especially when they were not at full capacity, ruined our experience.

We had other staff double checking what we had ordered, it felt like it was the first night they had opened.

When we complained we had other staff tell us it would be ready when it was cooked. This is completely fine and I understand this, but they should then therefore make this explicitly clear when ordering. If we would have known that we would have ordered differently.

They did deduct 10% from our bill as a goodwill gesture. But I'd be hesitant to return to be completely honest.

issues: A very strong week with sales of £43,000; delivery was down a little.
Covers are still at December levels, but voucher offer volume has dropped off: the site did 6,575 ramens with 2,300 covers last week.
Labour figures do not match: Kobas shows 669 hours against 769 hours on the sheet, which the GM will look into; training hours and a team meeting were also used last week.
Food cost was 30.9%, a little over the 30% target, but there is now a good buffer and the GM and Mag think they can bring it back down.
Stock variance was unusually high and above the 5% limit: lemonade showed a 1,271% variance, even before counting an off brand lemonade postmix found in the stock room that nobody can explain.

Cans were also up (32 Coke, 23 Coke Zero and 15 Diet Coke) because Jimmy bought cans from Tesco to cover a busy delivery weekend, and stock brought over from Birmingham (Red Bull, orange juice and pineapple juice) still needs a stock transfer.
Matcha appeared on the stock list for the first time and shows half a bag up (about £20 of variance), and Maki Biru light is about £20 up, probably a miscount.
Amy asked the GM to check the lemonade deliveries against invoices, log the Tesco purchases as a random buy in, and fix this week's variance.
Wages were 25.3%, better than expected; the extra staff made shifts run more smoothly than in recent weeks.
Delivery is moving in the right direction, though Tuesday and Thursday were the worst days last week.
Reviews: 43 last week, including two 2 stars; one, from the week before, said food did not come out at the same time, and the other said the hell seafood ramen tasted bad and was too spicy.
The GM will go through all complaint reviews with Caitlyn tomorrow, reply to them and offer invite backs.

Maintenance: the toilets should now be fixed, but the GM needs to check the treatment report on whether the drains need flushing or just bleaching; the beer cooler gas canister is still playing up, there is a hole in the bar floor, and a new pot wash is coming.
Staffing: Samantha and Duni are on board and can both work full time; Amy will hire one more full time FOH, with a trial shift tomorrow at 12:00.
An AGM has been hired from last week's trial and is going through onboarding, with training first; Amy will confirm the start date with Inka.
Events: a cocktail night on Wednesday with Inka and Amarian making cocktails at Fusion, and a Panthers versus Cardiff ice hockey game this Friday, expected to bring in local and out of town trade.
B2B: student accommodation events are planned for mid November (date not yet confirmed) and 30/11; Amy will attend and asked for one staff member to go with her for now.
A new delivery scanning pack is being sent to Nottingham, to be placed in the bar area to cut rider waiting time.
Scratch cards produced only one or two redemptions overall in regions 10 and 16 as well as Leicester, and will not be carried forward (Admin Meeting 26/10).
O and Amy are mainly focusing on Nottingham's Deliveroo performance this week (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Nottingham drove strong venue bookings from Google ads (Weekly DPM Meeting 27/10).

Region: the new Christmas set menu (including a set menu for large bookings) brings three new dishes; head chefs must check stock and have everything ready by Friday 30/10, leaflets must be ready by Friday (nudge marketing if they are late) and an allergy sheet is needed for the new dishes.

Region: the £5 ramen promotion ends on Saturday 31/10, and a new loyalty tier promotion will follow, probably announced at next Tuesday's KPI meeting.
